proposals.before: Two years later, Liu Ze sent a messenger to tell Tian Sheng: 'I will not help you anymore.'
proposals.after: In the second year, Liu Ze sent a messenger to tell Tian Sheng: 'I will not help you anymore.'
proposals.reason: Chinese 二年 in this annalistic sequence after 高后時 marks Empress Lü year 2, not a relative "two years later."

proposals.before: The Han King then commanded Liu Jia to lead the Jiujiang troops southwest with Grand Marshal Lu Wan to attack King Linjiang Gong Wei.
proposals.after: The Han King then commanded Liu Jia to lead the Jiujiang troops southwest with Grand Commandant Lu Wan to attack King Linjiang Gong Wei.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant; rendering it Grand Marshal conflates it with 大司馬 used earlier for Zhou Yin.

proposals.before: Dingguo wished to have an official killed—the magistrate of Feiru, a man from Ying. When this man and others reported Dingguo's crimes, Dingguo had the court usher bring trumped-up charges against them, arresting and killing the man from Ying to silence him.
proposals.after: Dingguo wished to kill an official, Yingren the magistrate of Feiru. When Yingren and others reported Dingguo's crimes, Dingguo had the court usher bring trumped-up charges against them, arresting and killing Yingren to silence him.
proposals.reason: 肥如令郢人 treats 郢人 as the official's name/designation, not a vague demonym "a man from Ying."

decisions.reason: In this annalistic stretch, 二年 is the second year of the reign already in force (高后時), not a relative span after the gold gift; "Two years later" misreads the dating formula, and "In the second year" restores it.
The unit has 太尉盧綰, while s0006 has 大司馬周殷; Grand Marshal for 太尉 conflates the offices, and Grand Commandant matches 太尉 and the idiomatic of this same unit.

decisions.after: Dingguo wished to have an official killed—Yingren, the magistrate of Feiru. When Yingren and others reported Dingguo's crimes, Dingguo had the court usher bring trumped-up charges against them, arresting and killing Yingren to silence him.
decisions.reason: 肥如令郢人 names the official 郢人 (Yingren), not a demonym "man from Ying"; the proposal is right on that point but awkwardly rewrites the verb and drops the em-dash apposition, so the repair keeps the original phrasing while substituting the personal name throughout.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 肥如令郢人，郢人等告定國
